problem: Split fine-tuning exchanges activations and gradients at every step, making communication a bottleneck for edge clients.
contribution: AE-PSL aligns an autoencoder with pretrained features and local client data before freezing it for compressed parallel split fine-tuning.
reading_guide: Read global results with the autoencoder bypassed at inference separately from local FEMNIST results with compression still active.

diagram.title: Align twice, then fine-tune
diagram.description: General alignment trains the autoencoder on public features. Clients adapt it locally and average only the decoders. Fine-tuning then uses local frozen encoders and one frozen server decoder, with compressed activations sent forward and latent gradients returned.

stages.title: General alignment
stages.detail: Train the autoencoder to reconstruct public split-layer features while the pretrained client partition stays frozen.

stages.title: Client alignment
stages.detail: Adapt locally; retain client encoders and average decoders into one server module.

stages.title: Split fine-tuning
stages.detail: Freeze compressors; exchange compact patch activations and gradients while adapting the split model.

diagram.footnote: The classification token and its gradient remain uncompressed. Predictions return to clients for local loss computation; the server aggregates losses before returning cut-layer gradients.

results.title: Global accuracy at about 10× reduction
results.question: Can compressed training preserve accuracy when the compressor is removed for global inference?
results.context: ViT-B/32, split layer 5, five clients, Dirichlet α=0.5; top-1 accuracy (%), higher is better. Mean ± standard deviation over three seeds. Compressed methods use R≈10; the reference uses R=1.
results.interpretation: At this reduction and client count, AE-PSL stays within 0.5 percentage points of the uncompressed reference on all three global benchmarks.
results.caveat: These are global tests after client-weight aggregation with the autoencoder bypassed. They do not measure compressed inference accuracy or full preparation cost.

results.title: Local inference under stronger compression
results.question: What happens when the compression bottleneck remains active at test time?
results.context: FEMNIST, ViT-B/32, 25 clients, writer-based partitions; local accuracy (%) averaged across clients, higher is better. Mean ± standard deviation over three seeds. Compressed methods use R≈20; reference R=1.
results.interpretation: AE-PSL has the highest reported accuracy among the compressed methods, 1.2 percentage points below the uncompressed reference.
results.caveat: FEMNIST uses 10% subsamples per writer and local tests. Its scores are not interchangeable with the centralized global tests above.

results.title: Why alignment and freezing matter
results.question: Does inserting an unaligned autoencoder fail in every evaluation mode?
results.context: ViT-B/32, five clients; R≈15 for all AE variants, R=1 for the reference. Accuracy (%) with reported ± terms over three seeds. GA: general alignment; CSA: client alignment; FZ: frozen autoencoder.
results.interpretation: Alignment and freezing restore compatibility with uncompressed global inference. An unaligned AE does not cause the same collapse when it remains active locally.
results.caveat: This is a separate ablation at R≈15. Its baseline values and reported spreads differ from Table 4, so the two tables should not be combined into one estimate.

evaluation.label: Data
evaluation.value: CIFAR-100, Food101, SUN397 and FEMNIST; public ImageNet100 for general alignment.

evaluation.label: Model
evaluation.value: ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/32, default split layer 5, two-layer MLP autoencoder; LoRA rank 16.

evaluation.label: Training
evaluation.value: 5 or 25 clients; 10 fine-tuning epochs, global batch 125; 30 general-alignment epochs and one local alignment epoch.

evaluation.label: Compared with
evaluation.value: Uncompressed training, Rand-Top-K, C3-SL and ADC, adapted to the same aggregated parallel split framework.

limitations: The evaluated downstream tasks are vision classification; non-vision, language-model and multimodal adaptation are not tested.
The design relies on an uncompressed classification token. Compressing it damages accuracy in the appendix ablation.
The principal global tests bypass the AE at inference; local FEMNIST uses a different evaluation protocol with it active.
Client GFLOP comparisons include local warm-up, but do not establish total system latency, energy savings or the amortized cost of 30-epoch public alignment.
takeaways: Learned compression needs to preserve the pretrained feature space, particularly if the compressor will later be removed.
The result is a measured accuracy–communication trade-off: stronger compression can reduce accuracy, and the inference protocol matters.
